candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a hypodense intraluminal mass with calcification nearly obliterating the main and hilar pulmonary arteries without peripheral extension, in a young woman — features more consistent with a primary pulmonary artery sarcoma (intimal sarcoma) than chronic thromboembolic disease. While chronic PE is a key differential and shares imaging overlap (filling defect, perfusion abnormality, elevated D-dimer), the reference diagnosis is specifically intimal sarcoma. Chronic PE is a related but incompatible final diagnosis because it asserts a thromboembolic rather than neoplastic etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Chronic pulmonary embolism is a thromboembolic entity; intimal sarcoma of the pulmonary artery is a primary malignant neoplasm — both can mimic each other radiologically but are distinct diagnostic entities with incompatible etiology and nature

case_quality_flags: Classic intimal sarcoma vs. chronic PE diagnostic mimicry case; calcification within mass and young age favor sarcoma over thrombus
